research.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
research.why: Reasoning models over-think, which costs time and money for every user; this proposes a way to make them stop once they have enough information. Easy for a general reader to follow, has a primary source, and is not a repeat of anything in the last 8 weeks. Caveat: scored from the abstract only (HF Daily Papers was the only research source), so the writer must read the full paper and report the actual accuracy/length trade-off.

runnersUp.title: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena
runnersUp.reason: Highest score (18) and strongest momentum, but it asks nearly the same question as 'Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?' (research, 2026-10-21), so it would repeat that issue's angle without a material update. Also check the arXiv ID: 2610.x on a Nov 4 HF listing suggests it was posted in October.

runnersUp.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
runnersUp.reason: Solid analysis paper, but harder to explain to a general reader.

runnersUp.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
runnersUp.reason: Interesting, but another agent benchmark, and agent evaluations ran on 2026-10-10 and 2026-11-04.

news.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Small
news.why: A new model from a major lab that will be released with open weights (Apache 2.0) after outside safety testing. Clearly inside the window, primary page fetched, strong HN discussion (281 pts). Caveat: the weights are only promised for next week, so describe it as closed for now. Its Artificial Analysis score of 31 is the lab's own citation, so attribute it.

runnersUp.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: 15-second video, lower pricing
runnersUp.reason: Equal score and highest momentum, but the Nov 6 date was guessed from the HN post time and never confirmed. It is also an incremental update (longer clips, lower price).

runnersUp.title: Claude gets a Personal Finance tool
runnersUp.reason: Useful to consumers, but little traction (HN 11 pts) and less significant than a new model release.

runnersUp.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber cybersecurity model
runnersUp.reason: Primary page returned 403 and the release date may fall before the window.

invention.title: Linum P-JiT: a text-to-image model trained for about $21K, Apache 2.0 weights
invention.why: A two-person lab training a usable 2B-parameter image model for about $21K and opening the code and weights shows a general reader that good models are no longer only for big companies. Primary field notes fetched, HN 270 pts. Caveat: cost and efficiency numbers (4x shorter attention context, 11x fewer samples) are company-reported, so attribute them and check the limitations section and sample quality.

runnersUp.title: Stroq: local audit of what your coding agent did and why
runnersUp.reason: Useful idea, but README not yet checked, and agent oversight tools ran recently (Sphinx, 2026-10-21).

runnersUp.title: Rivet: scale and orchestrate agents on S3
runnersUp.reason: Launch HN post that reads as promotion; infrastructure that matters mostly to developers.

thread: Each piece shows AI getting cheaper: a reasoning model taught to stop thinking once it has enough, a lab releasing a small model with open weights, and a two-person team training an image model for about $21K.
